name: Performance Stats
description: Turn on the worldserver's own timing instrumentation, so `.perf cpu` and `.perf memory` report real numbers, and set how often its interval timer fires.

keys.note: World.cpp:1562 reads this into CONFIG_BOOL_PERFORMANCE_ENABLE; World.cpp:846 copies it into g_bEnableStatGather, which is what XStatTimer::Begin/End check before recording anything (Timer.h:189-190). THIS is the key with the visible effect.
seconds between interval reports; World.cpp:1575, and `.perf intervalreport` with no argument prints it back. See the notes: the handler it fires is empty on this fork.

patches.note: the line this fork ships at /opt/tortoise/etc/mangosd.conf:2193
the line this fork ships at /opt/tortoise/etc/mangosd.conf:2196

notes: The one manifest on this fork whose key the running server states back on its own
console. `.perf intervalreport` with no argument prints `Performance report interval is
<n>` from sWorld.getConfig(CONFIG_UINT32_PERFORMANCE_REPORT_INTERVAL)
(src/game/Commands/Commands.cpp:19146-19154), and its command row is
{ "intervalreport", SEC_ADMINISTRATOR, true, ... } (src/game/Chat/Chat.cpp:837) -- the
`true` is allowConsole, so the mangosd console answers with no client and no character.
It prints the value and THEN returns false, so the console follows it with `Incorrect
syntax.`; that second line is the fork's own and is not an error about the value.
WHAT EACH KEY REALLY DOES, measured on m910q 2026-09-08 rather than assumed from the name:
`Perf.Enable` is the load-bearing one. It becomes g_bEnableStatGather (World.cpp:846), which
XStatTimer::Begin/End check before recording (Timer.h:189-190), so with it off `.perf cpu`
and `.perf memory` report nothing. With it on they report real per-map update, movement and
spell timings -- that is this item's visible effect, and it needs no client.
`Perf.ReportInterval` sets the timer that fires PerformanceMonitor::ReportPerformanceToDB(),
and ON THIS FORK'S HEAD THAT FUNCTION IS EMPTY (PerformanceMonitor.cpp:180-183). So changing
the interval today changes what the console reports and nothing else. It is still worth
setting -- it is the value the server states back, and it is what the number will mean when
upstream fills the function in -- but do not expect periodic lines in the log because of it.
This fork has NO `.server motd` command at all (its serverCommandTable is
corpses/exit/idlerestart/idleshutdown/info/resetallraids/restart/shutdown,
src/game/Chat/Chat.cpp:700-711), which is why the TBC set's `motd` could not be this
game's proof and this item was written instead.
mangosd reads etc/mangosd.conf at startup, so the value arrives on the restart this item
asks for. `.reload config` also exists on this fork (Chat.cpp:553) and re-runs
LoadConfigSettingsFromFile, so a restart is sufficient rather than the only route.
